name: Laugavegur trail
region: Fjallabak Nature Reserve to Þórsmörk, south highlands
why: Four days from the striped rhyolite hills of Landmannalaugar over obsidian and snow, past a green lake and black sand deserts, down into the birch woods of Þórsmörk.
book: Open about 25 June to 15 September. Book the Ferðafélag Íslands huts or campsites months ahead (fi.is): you are expected to have a bed or a pitch for every night. Highland bus to Landmannalaugar and back from Þórsmörk; parking at Landmannalaugar must be reserved.
water: Streams and hut taps are drinkable; the small shops at Landmannalaugar and Þórsmörk sell little, carry food for all four days.
dangers: Fog and snowfields between Landmannalaugar and Álftavatn: people have died off the marked route, stay on it and carry a GPS track.
Snow bridges over the ravines near Hrafntinnusker can collapse: walk around them.
At least three rivers to wade (Grashagakvísl, Bláfjallakvísl, Þröngá): sandals, waist strap open, cross in the morning when they run lower.
Storms with wind over 15 m/s even in July: check vedur.is and register your plan on safetravel.is.
turnaround: Do not leave a hut into fog or a forecast wind over 15 m/s: wait a day, the wardens know.

points.name: Landmannalaugar hut
points.note: 600 m, by the hot spring. The trail climbs at once through the Laugahraun lava past Brennisteinsalda's coloured slopes and steam vents.

points.name: Hrafntinnusker hut
points.note: About 1,050 m, the highest and coldest night: obsidian on the ground, snow most of the summer, steam from the vents behind the hut.

points.name: Álftavatn hut
points.note: After the steep descent of Jökultungur: the green lake under moss-covered ridges, two huts on the shore.

points.name: Emstrur (Botnar) hut
points.note: After the black sands of Mælifellssandur. Ten minutes from the huts, the Markarfljótsgljúfur canyon drops 180 m.

points.name: Þórsmörk, Langidalur hut
points.note: Birch woods after the Þröngá ford, the Krossá braids under Eyjafjallajökull. Buses leave from Langidalur and Húsadalur.
